text:
IncidentBot: ALERT: sudden p99 latency spike detected across kv-cache-serv shards [12,13,14] — p95 ~450ms -> 1.6s, p99 ~2.3s -> 8.1s in the last 7m. Streaming tail stalls + high number of streaming timeouts. SLO (generation-api) crossing 5s p99. Paging oncall @Ana (oncall) :rotating_light:
Ana (oncall): Seeing it. Confirming impact on hosted inference routes: /v1/generate and /v1/stream. Any recent rollouts?@deploy-bot?
deploy-bot: No releases in the last 30m. Canary traffic stable.
Kai: I can pick this up. Starting quick triage: checking kv-cache eviction rates and prefill queues.
Rishi: Copy. I’ll look at node-level metrics and anything unusual in kernel OOM/IO.
Nina: I’m watching customer-facing dashboards; two customers show elevated tail latencies and a retry surge. Recommending we mark incident and notify CS if we need mitigations that may change perf.
SRE-Triage: Assigning Sev: potential SLO breach. Triage owners: Kai (exec), Rishi (infra), Ana (pager).
Kai: Early hypothesis: KV cache pressure causing fragmentation. Prefill workers appear to be enqueueing more prefill jobs than decode workers can consume -> prefill backlog and lock contention. This creates long waits for streaming decode path.
Kai: quick check logs (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] shard=13 prefill.enqueue latency=1.5ms queue_len=1820
[2026-03-15T09:12:10Z] shard=13 decode.worker.wait=987ms active_decodes=6
[2026-03-15T09:12:18Z] shard=13 eviction.triggered reason=fragmentation candidates=240
[2026-03-15T09:12:43Z] streaming.write stall=3200ms client=hosting-42
```
Rishi: Node-level snapshot: CPU ~65% but swap usage creeping on 2 nodes, dentry cache growing small, I/O wait spikes on nvme. Might be memory pressure from prefills (large key blobs).
Ana (oncall): Immediate mitigation options? Can we throttle prefill or divert traffic to less-affected shards/regions?
Kai: We can flip prefill throttling flag per-shard to cap new prefill jobs and prioritize decode. Patch to change `PREFILL_MAX_INFLIGHT` to 50 from 500 for shards 12-14.
Kai: Proposed live command (rolling):
```
# throttle prefill on affected shards
curl -XPOST https://control-plane.internal/kv/prefill/throttle -d '{"shards":[12,13,14],"max_inflight":50}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN"
```
Rishi: Also recommend increasing decode worker pool on those nodes by +2 each and force a lightweight cache compaction sweep. I’ll run: `kubectl scale deployment/decode-worker --replicas=$CURRENT+2 -l shard in (12,13,14)`
Ana (oncall): Sounds good. Deploy-bot? Any risk with scaling decode workers now?
deploy-bot: Scaling decode-worker is allowed; image pinned, metrics alarms suppressed for 10m during scale.
Nina: If we throttle prefill, customer throughput could dip briefly. CS should be looped if we trigger any manual throttles.
Ana (oncall): I’ll notify CS and post a short customer-facing note if mitigation affects latency. Nina, can you draft?
Nina: On it. Draft: "We're investigating increased latency affecting some generation requests; applying targeted mitigations to stabilize tail latency. We'll provide updates within 30 minutes."
Kai: Executing prefill throttle now.
SRE-Triage: ACTION: Kai -> POST throttle, Rishi -> scale decode + run cache compaction, Ana -> customer comms and incident timeline.
Kai: POSTed throttle. Response: {"status":"accepted","job_id":"throttle-3945"}. Prefill enqueue rate dropped ~70% within 30s.
Rishi: Scaling decode workers now. `kubectl scale` returned success. Starting compaction sweep (low-priority).
Ana (oncall): Noting in incident timeline. Current p99 after throttle: 3.1s (down from 8.1s). Streaming stalls count reduced by ~45%. Still above SLO.
Kai: Good partial improvement. Next step: reduce eviction aggressiveness to avoid mid-request evictions. Patch candidate to bump `EVICTION_HEADROOM` from 5% -> 12% on the three shards. I’ll prepare a short rollout to change shard config with automatic rollback if errors.
Rishi: Compaction sweep reports: reclaimed ~18% KV index fragments on shard 13, IO pressure easing. No OOMs.
Ana (oncall): OK. Execute EVICTION_HEADROOM patch if you think it’s safe. We want to avoid causing cache thrashing.
Kai: Rolling change applied to shard config. Monitoring.
deploy-bot: Config change applied to shards [12,13,14] via config-service v2. Rollout id: cfg-7892.
Nina: Customer note ready, sending to CS slack.
Ana (oncall): p99 now ~1.2s, p95 ~360ms. Streaming stalls back to baseline. Looks like throttle + scale + compaction did it.
SRE-Triage: Reduce severity to watching. Keep monitoring for 60m. Prepare handoff notes for next oncall.
Kai: Summary for handoff: root cause likely prefill/ decode skew + KV fragmentation under sudden burst. Mitigations applied: 1) per-shard prefill throttle, 2) increased decode workers, 3) cache compaction sweep, 4) increased eviction headroom.
Ana (oncall): Handoff note (to next oncall): monitor shards 12-14, watch prefill queue length, decode worker backlog, p99 for generation-api and streaming stalls metric. If p99 climbs >3s again: revert prefill throttle (if underprovisioning) or temporarily route traffic away from affected shards using routing-policy 'avoid-shard-12-14'.
Rishi: I captured node-level traces and logs to /internal/incidents/3945678901/ for postmortem. Adding initial timeline and metrics.
SRE-Triage: CS notified. Incident downgraded to SEV-WATCH. Will create ticket for long-term fixes: better prefill backpressure, smarter eviction heuristics, and prefill size capping.
Ana (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving handoff to Kai (until 10:30Z) and Rishi (infra). I’m done with active pager.
Kai: I’ll keep an eye on metrics for the next 30m.
Nina: CS confirmed customer note sent. No escalations so far.
SRE-Triage: Closing active page. Logging incident as 3945678901-kv-prefill-decode-skew. Postmortem assigned to Kai + Rishi.
Ana (oncall): Good job everyone :thumbsup:
